scope: Proposition 7.5 (Pure-collision cutting alternatives, imported) of the manuscript “Hard-sphere fluctuations on the regular Boltzmann lifespan” (preprints/Hard-sphere-fluctuations-on-the-regular-Boltzmann-lifespan-September-23-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 364 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 e294d8e5097f8d0e), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF pages 44-45. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. statement: Let M be a connected, full, realizable graph containing only scattering contacts. Full means that all its end variables are integrated. Define a transversal set A ⊂ M to be a set for which M \ A = A− ⊔ A+, with no directed bond from A+ to A ∪ A−, or from A to A−. Let X0(A) consist of vertices outside A with two bonds to A, and let X(A) be the closure obtained by repeatedly adding vertices with two bonds to the set already grown. The following statements hold; in parts (ii)–(iv), A is assumed to be connected. (i) There is a chain of connected transversal sets A1, . . . , Am = M, with A1 a tree, such that X0(Aj) ̸= ∅ for j < m, Aj ∪ X(Aj) ⊂ Aj+1, r(Aj+1) = r(Aj ∪ X(Aj)), r(Aj+1) − r(Aj) ≤ 10|X(Aj)|. The intermediate growth from Aj ∪ X(Aj) to Aj+1 adds one bond at each new vertex. For any D transitions in this chain there is a cutting sequence of all of M with one type {4}, no type {44} or type-B pair, and at least D type-A pairs. (ii) One can choose A± such that each component of A+ is attached to A. The two parts X±(A) = X(A) ∩ A± are equivalently obtained by adding vertices with two predecessors, or two successors, in the grown set. They are convex along particle lines. If m± is the number of bonds from A to X±(A), then |X± (A)| ≤ G(m±), G(q) = (2q + 1) ( q 2 ) (32q3/2 )q2 (q ≥ 2). The harmless values G(0), G(1) may be replaced by one. (iii) Put z = |X± 0 (A)| and a = r(A). There is a cutting sequence of M having one type {4}, no type {44} or type-B pair, and at least z/2 − a − 1 type-A pairs. (iv) For this same choice of side there is a finite Borel partition of the contact-parameter domain, with a subcase-dependent integer y ≥ 0, and the following two available sequences in each subcase: HARD-SPHERE FLUCTUATIONS 45 • a sequence with one type {4}, no type {44} or type-B pair, and at least y/10 − 3(a + 1) uniformly good singletons; • a sequence with no type {44}, at most S = a + z + y type {4} singletons, all type-B pairs uniformly good, and at least m± − 105S 10 type-A or type-B pairs in total. The singleton and pair types not counted for a gain have the neutral kernels described above. On graphs of polylogarithmic size and bounded excess the indicated partitions and operation sequences have at most Cb| log ϵ|C∗ subcases. The exponential base C depends on dimensional choices, not on L. The required local restrictions at each uniformly good piece involve its own variables and data exposed earlier in the cutting order.
